 Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX) Merger Talks Raise The Question Of Whether Shares Are A Bargain
 AL Al Bentley November 20, 2026, 11:12 UTC Share Tesla and Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX) are reportedly deep in merger talks over a proposed deal above US$3.5 trillion, a potential tie up that immediately reframes how investors think about SPCX’s AI, space and mobility ambitions.
 Space Exploration Technologies has slipped over the year, with the 90 day share price return slightly positive at 1.1% while the year to date share price return is down 14.0%. This suggests recent merger headlines and heavy AI data center spending are not yet reversing a broader cooling in momentum.
 Spot emerging peers to Space Exploration Technologies by scanning our hand picked 53 AI infrastructure stocks , which are also leaning hard into AI-driven compute and connectivity.
 Space Exploration Technologies now trades well below many analyst models, yet carries a market value near US$2.0t and heavy AI spend already in the price. How much of the long term opportunity is still not reflected in today’s valuation?
 Advertisement Most Popular Narrative: 33% Undervalued
 Against a last close of $138.43, the most followed narrative pins Space Exploration Technologies’ fair value at $207.00. This frames the current pullback as a sizeable gap to that scenario.
 According to deyan_89mg6, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community who wrote the narrative, the business is no longer just about rockets and broadband. It is assessed as a vertically integrated platform spanning launch, connectivity, AI compute, software and semiconductor infrastructure, with long term equity value tied to how those layers interact rather than any single product line.
 SpaceX should no longer be viewed primarily as a launch company. Its emerging structure is more appropriately analyzed as a vertically integrated infrastructure platform built around Space, Connectivity, and AI. The investment case therefore depends less on launch revenue alone and increasingly on the interaction between Starship, Starlink, Starlink Mobile, AI compute, software, and semiconductor infrastructure. 
 See why 89 investors see Space Exploration Technologies as 33% undervalued .
 The narrative applies a 7.236% discount rate to those future cash flow scenarios and arrives at a fair value that is about 33.1% above where SPCX shares last traded. That gap is materially wider than the 46.2% discount implied by the average analyst price target of $257.50, and well below the $367.05 estimate from the SWS DCF model that prices in even more optimistic cash generation. Compared with those anchors, the narrative sits in the middle, treating the current $1.95b market capitalization as leaving room for upside but still demanding strong execution across AI compute, Starlink Mobile and Terafab.
 Result: Fair Value of $207.00 (UNDERVALUED) 
 Still, heavy AI capex that fails to earn its keep, along with any disappointment in Starlink Mobile economics, could quickly undercut the prevailing Space Exploration Technologies thesis.
